chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Musa ibn al-Qasim, from Ali ibn Ja'far, from his brother Abu al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him), said:

I asked him about raisins: is it permissible to cook them until their flavor is extracted, then that water is taken and cooked until two-thirds of it evaporates and one-third remains, then it is removed and drunk from it for the year? He said: There is no problem with it.

key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ بِهِ: There is no problem with it (permissible)

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to cook raisins and reduce the liquid to make a concentrated sweetener in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam Musa al-Kazim (AS) clarifies the permissibility of 'Tala'a' by validating a specific preparation method where raisins are boiled to extract flavor, and the liquid is reduced to one-third for year-round consumption. It highlights the scholarly distinction between simple grape juice reduction and this infused variant, ensuring the final product remains within the bounds of halal consumption without becoming intoxicating.
